3 Lessons from Advertising Week 2026 for Dental and Medical Marketing

By Patrick Hounsell, Co-CEO · October 9, 2026

Advertising Week New York 2026 had three lessons that matter for every dental and medical practice owner who spends money on marketing.

I spent four days in New York listening to the people who run the biggest ad budgets in the world. Most of it was about brands far larger than a dental office. But three themes kept coming up, and every one of them applies to a local practice right now.

Key takeaways

  • Connected TV is now local and measurable.
  • Reviews and trust decide who gets the booking.
  • AI assistants are starting to book, not just recommend.
Lesson 1Lesson 2

Lesson 1: TV is now a local, measurable channel

Streaming TV lets a practice show an ad only to households near its office and count the visits that follow.

According to the 2026 CTV report, streaming passed 47% of all TV viewing time this year.

Lesson 2: You can't have performance without trust

Patients read reviews before they call. A practice with fewer than 50 reviews loses the click to the one down the street.

"Trust is the new targeting."

Frequently asked questions

What is connected TV (CTV) advertising?

CTV advertising is a video ad shown on a streaming service watched on a TV, such as Hulu or YouTube on a smart TV.
